answer.rationale: Finance mandates an 18% spend cut and the incumbent has refused to reopen price. Memory c2 records that switching to the low-cost vendor previously cut unit cost sharply with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing — directly applicable to meeting the mandated cost reduction. Memory c4 shows that benchmarking against market rates recovered margin at renewal, which supports moving off a vendor that refuses to negotiate. Switching primary supply is feasible with 14 days left (c2 onboarding was quick) and reduces dependence on a vendor that has signaled no price flexibility. Delivery risk is mitigated by the existing line running at 94% of committed volume with no buffer, so a transition must be tightly sequenced — but the prior success with the low-cost vendor suggests it can be executed without disruption. The other candidates (renew, defer, add second source, negotiate terms) either fail the cost objective given the incumbent's stance or don't fully address the mandated cut within one cycle.
